nodes.label: Gaia
nodes.description: The Earth herself, who emerged after Chaos and bore the sky, the mountains and the sea.

nodes.label: Uranus
nodes.description: The starry sky, husband of Gaia, overthrown and castrated by his son Cronus.

nodes.label: Nyx
nodes.description: Night itself, a power so old that even Zeus feared to anger her.

nodes.label: Eris
nodes.description: Goddess of strife whose golden apple "for the fairest" set off the Trojan War.

nodes.label: Oceanus
nodes.description: The great river encircling the world, father of all rivers and springs.

nodes.label: Tethys
nodes.description: Titaness of fresh water and mother of the river gods and the Oceanids.

nodes.label: Hyperion
nodes.description: Titan of heavenly light and father of the Sun, the Moon and the Dawn.

nodes.label: Theia
nodes.description: Titaness of sight and brilliance who gave gold and gems their shine.

nodes.label: Coeus
nodes.description: Titan of inquiring intellect, grandfather of Apollo and Artemis.

nodes.label: Phoebe
nodes.description: Titaness who held the Delphic oracle before passing it to her grandson Apollo.

nodes.label: Cronus
nodes.description: Youngest Titan, who deposed his father and swallowed his own children.

nodes.label: Rhea
nodes.description: Mother of the Olympians, who saved Zeus by giving Cronus a swaddled stone.

nodes.label: Iapetus
nodes.description: Titan father of Prometheus and Atlas, ancestor of humankind.

nodes.label: Themis
nodes.description: Titaness of divine order and custom, second wife of Zeus.

nodes.label: Mnemosyne
nodes.description: Titaness of memory, who bore Zeus the nine Muses.

nodes.label: Helios
nodes.description: The Sun, who drives his fiery chariot across the sky and sees everything.

nodes.label: Selene
nodes.description: The Moon, who rides the night sky in a silver chariot.

nodes.label: Eos
nodes.description: The rosy-fingered Dawn who opens the gates of heaven every morning.

nodes.label: Leto
nodes.description: Titaness hunted by jealous Hera, who gave birth to Apollo and Artemis on Delos.

nodes.label: Metis
nodes.description: First wife of Zeus; he swallowed her while she was pregnant with Athena.

nodes.label: Prometheus
nodes.description: Titan who stole fire for humanity and was chained to a rock for it.

nodes.label: Atlas
nodes.description: Titan condemned to hold up the sky at the western edge of the world.

nodes.label: Maia
nodes.description: Eldest of the Pleiades, who bore Hermes in a cave on Mount Cyllene.

nodes.label: Zeus
nodes.description: King of the gods, who overthrew Cronus and rules from Mount Olympus.

nodes.label: Hera
nodes.description: Queen of the gods and protector of marriage, famously jealous of Zeus’s lovers.

nodes.label: Poseidon
nodes.description: Lord of the sea and the shaker of the earth.

nodes.label: Demeter
nodes.description: Goddess of grain, whose grief for Persephone brings the winter.

nodes.label: Hestia
nodes.description: Eldest Olympian and keeper of the hearth fire, honoured first at every sacrifice.

nodes.label: Hades
nodes.description: Ruler of the dead, who drew the underworld when the brothers divided the cosmos.

nodes.label: Athena
nodes.description: Goddess of wisdom and strategy, born fully armed from the head of Zeus.

nodes.label: Apollo
nodes.description: God of music, light and prophecy, who speaks through the oracle at Delphi.

nodes.label: Artemis
nodes.description: Virgin huntress and protector of wild animals, twin sister of Apollo.

nodes.label: Ares
nodes.description: God of the violence and bloodlust of war.

nodes.label: Aphrodite
nodes.description: Goddess of love, born from the sea foam where Uranus’s severed flesh fell.

nodes.label: Hephaestus
nodes.description: Smith of the gods, who forged Zeus’s thunderbolts and Achilles’s armour.

nodes.label: Hermes
nodes.description: Messenger of the gods and guide of souls, a thief on the day he was born.

nodes.label: Dionysus
nodes.description: God of wine and ecstasy, the only Olympian with a mortal mother.

nodes.label: Persephone
nodes.description: Queen of the underworld, who returns to her mother every spring.

nodes.label: Hebe
nodes.description: Goddess of youth and cupbearer of the gods, later wife of the deified Heracles.

nodes.label: Eileithyia
nodes.description: Goddess of childbirth, who could hasten or delay any birth.

nodes.label: The Muses
nodes.description: Nine daughters of Zeus and Memory who inspire poetry, music and learning.

nodes.label: Eros
nodes.description: God of desire whose arrows make gods and mortals fall in love.

nodes.label: Harmonia
nodes.description: Daughter of War and Love, whose cursed wedding necklace doomed her descendants.

nodes.label: Amphitrite
nodes.description: Sea goddess and queen of the waves, wife of Poseidon.

nodes.label: Triton
nodes.description: Merman herald of the sea, who calms or raises the waves with his conch.

nodes.label: Asclepius
nodes.description: God of medicine, struck down by Zeus for raising the dead.

nodes.label: Cadmus
nodes.description: Founder of Thebes and bringer of the alphabet to Greece, husband of Harmonia.

nodes.label: Semele
nodes.description: Theban princess who burned to ash on seeing Zeus in his true form.

nodes.label: Alcmene
nodes.description: Mortal queen whom Zeus visited disguised as her own husband.

nodes.label: Danaë
nodes.description: Princess locked in a bronze chamber, whom Zeus reached as a shower of gold.

nodes.label: Leda
nodes.description: Spartan queen whom Zeus seduced in the form of a swan.

nodes.label: Heracles
nodes.description: Greatest of heroes, who completed twelve labours and was made a god.

nodes.label: Perseus
nodes.description: Hero who beheaded Medusa and rescued Andromeda.

nodes.label: Helen
nodes.description: Most beautiful of women, whose abduction to Troy launched a thousand ships.
